# Privacy notice

Use this template alongside the [consent form](./consent-form.md). A privacy notice explains how personal data is handled; it is not itself consent and does not replace consent where consent is the legal basis. Replace every bracketed field, remove categories you do not collect, and have the responsible organisation and local adviser check the notice against applicable law.

The sections follow the information that data protection laws commonly require at collection. GDPR Article 13 is one detailed example: controller and contact details, purposes and legal basis, recipients, cross-border transfers, retention, data-subject rights, withdrawal of consent, the right to complain, and any automated decision-making ([GDPR Article 13](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-13-gdpr/)). African laws differ in detail; start from the [country reference](../legal-consent/index.md#data-protection-laws-in-africa-quick-country-reference) and check the law that applies to your project.

## Who is responsible

**Controller:** [Organisation or community responsible for deciding why and how personal data is processed, with contact details.]

**Processors and service providers:** [Categories such as hosting, storage, email, transcription or technical support. Name each provider in the published notice where required, and state the processing it performs.]

**Data protection or privacy contact:** [Named role and contact route.]

## What we collect and why

List only the categories the project actually uses. State the purpose and legal basis separately for each category rather than relying on one general statement.

| Data category | Purpose | Legal basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name, contact details and contributor code | Recruitment, coordination, support and attribution where chosen | [Basis for this category] |
| Consent records and form versions | Demonstrate permissions, restrictions and withdrawals | [Basis for this category] |
| Voice, image, text or other contributed content | [Collection, annotation, research or release purpose] | [Basis for this category] |
| Optional speaker profile, such as age band, gender and language varieties | [Analysis or release purpose; explain that answering is optional] | [Separate basis and consent version where applicable] |
| Language background, region and relevant expertise | Assignment, quality analysis and bias assessment | [Basis for this category] |
| Quality scores, review outcomes and access decisions | Training, review, safety and project administration | [Basis for this category] |
| Payment or compensation records, if contributors or annotators are paid | Paying people and meeting accounting or tax obligations | [Basis for this category] |
| IP addresses, device identifiers, connection and security logs | Security, troubleshooting and abuse prevention | [Basis for this category] |
| Accountability and audit logs | Record access, consent, policy and export decisions | [Basis for this category] |

Do not infer sensitive attributes or add new purposes merely because a field is available. Explain which questions are optional and what happens if someone declines. If quality scores or automated checks decide on their own who may join, keeps access or gets paid, say so, explain the logic in plain terms, and give a route to human review; some laws, such as the GDPR, set specific duties for automated decisions with significant effects ([GDPR Article 13](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-13-gdpr/)).

## Who can see the data

Describe visibility by role: contributors, annotators, reviewers, project managers, technical administrators, processors and the public. State whether annotators can see only assigned work, who can see identifiable profiles or quality records, and who may approve exports or support access. Do not publish member lists or individual quality records.

## Storage and international transfers

For each system or copy, state the provider or institution, storage location and country, and any other countries from which data may be accessed. Explain the safeguards and legal mechanism used for cross-border transfers where required. Link the operational inventory to [Know where every copy lives](../6_documentation/data-storage.md#know-where-every-copy-lives-and-for-how-long).

## Retention

Set a retention period or deletion rule for each category, including source content, labels, consent records, optional profiles, quality records, security logs, exports and backups. Explain what happens when a project is paused, archived or deleted. Do not use a single indefinite period for unlike records.

## Your rights and choices

Explain the rights available under the applicable law, which may include access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection, portability and withdrawal of consent. Give a working contact route, an identity-verification procedure that does not collect unnecessary documents, and the process for handling a request. Explain any lawful limits and how to complain to the relevant authority.

Under laws such as the GDPR (Article 7(3)) and South Africa's POPIA (section 11(2)(b)), withdrawing consent does not make processing before withdrawal unlawful ([European Union, 2016](../references.md#gdpr-2016); [POPIA section 11](https://popia.co.za/section-11-consent-justification-and-objection/)). Explain how withdrawal affects existing releases and future exports without promising that copies already obtained by others can always be recalled. See [Withdrawal](../legal-consent/index.md#withdrawal).

## Children and other contributors requiring assistance

State the minimum age or competency requirements used by the project, the applicable jurisdiction, and when consent from a parent, guardian or other legally competent person is required. Explain how that consent and the contributor's age category are recorded. Do not assume one threshold applies in every country or processing context; see [Contributors under the applicable age of consent](../legal-consent/index.md#contributors-under-the-applicable-age-of-consent).

## Changes to this notice

| Version and date | What changed | Contact or approval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Version and date] | [Summary] | [Responsible role] |

Material changes require renewed information and, where necessary, a new legal basis or fresh consent. Keep earlier notice versions with the consent records to which they relate.
